# Citations

All sources used in this research, numbered sequentially. Each entry includes
the specific data extracted and a source quality tier.

---

**[1]** "TOON Specification v3.0 (Working Draft)." *GitHub*, toon-format/spec, 2025.
<https://github.com/toon-format/spec>
**Tier:** 2
Data extracted: ABNF grammar, syntax rules (arrays, objects, nesting, quoting), media type `text/toon`, design goals ("compact, human-readable encoding of the JSON data model for LLM prompts"), v3.0 released 2025-11-24, MIT license, UTF-8 required.

**[2]** "Benchmarks." *TOON Format*, toonformat.dev, 2025.
<https://toonformat.dev/guide/benchmarks>
**Tier:** 2
Data extracted: 209 questions, 11 datasets, 4 models (claude-haiku-4-5, gemini-3-flash, gpt-5-nano, grok-4-1-fast), 5,016 LLM calls. Overall: TOON 76.4% accuracy / 2,759 tokens vs JSON 75.0% / 4,587 tokens. Mixed-structure track: TOON 227,830 vs JSON 291,711 tokens (−21.9%). Flat-only track: TOON 67,778 vs CSV 63,997 (+5.9%). Per-model accuracy breakdowns. Tokenizer: GPT-5 o200k_base.

**[3]** "Efficiency Formalization." *TOON Format*, toonformat.dev, 2025.
<https://toonformat.dev/reference/efficiency-formalization>
**Tier:** 2
Data extracted: Byte-level efficiency model Δ = L_json(Ω) − L_toon(Ω). Tabular arrays are TOON's optimal case. Arrays-of-arrays case reverses advantage (JSON more efficient). Model is "deliberately simplified."

**[4]** "TRON Format." *TRON Format*, tron-format.github.io, 2025.
<https://tron-format.github.io/>
**Tier:** 2
Data extracted: Site is a JavaScript SPA; static content did not render for fetch. Creator: Tim Huang. TRON is a JSON superset. Class syntax: `class A: a,b` then `A(1,2), A(3,4)`. Playground available at `#/playground`. MIT license.

**[5]** "tron-javascript." *GitHub*, tron-format/tron-javascript, 2025.
<https://github.com/tron-format/tron-javascript>
**Tier:** 2
Data extracted: JavaScript implementation, 18 stars, 2 forks. npm package `@tron-format/tron`. Creator: Tim Huang. Compression example: `[{"a":1,"b":2},{"a":3,"b":4}]` becomes `class A: a,b\nA(1,2), A(3,4)`.

**[6]** "ECMA-404: The JSON Data Interchange Syntax, 2nd Edition." *Ecma International*, December 2017.
<https://ecma-international.org/publications-and-standards/standards/ecma-404/>
**Tier:** 1
Data extracted: JSON standard, 2nd edition December 2017 (1st edition October 2013). Also ISO/IEC 21778. Lightweight text-based syntax derived from ECMAScript.

Data extracted: Current Internet Standard (STD 90) for JSON. Supersedes RFC 4627 (2006). Consistent with ECMA-404.

**[11]** Sikora, Piotr. "TOON vs TRON vs CSV vs YAML vs JSON Format Comparison." *piotr-sikora.com*, December 5, 2025.
<https://www.piotr-sikora.com/blog/2025-12-05-toon-tron-csv-yaml-json-format-comparison>
**Tier:** 3
Data extracted: 14 test scenarios with token counts per format. Overall savings vs JSON: CSV 80%, TOON 75%, TRON 60%, YAML 41%. Cost at scale (10K records, GPT-4): JSON $5.60, TRON $2.24, TOON $1.38, CSV $1.14. Context window capacity (128K): JSON ~17K records, TRON ~45K, TOON ~70K, CSV ~85K. Measurement basis: character counts and token approximations.

**[12]** Nandakishore, Gowthamkumar. "JTON: A Token-Efficient JSON Superset with Zen Grid Tabular Encoding for Large Language Models." *arXiv*, 2604.05865, March 2026.
<https://arxiv.org/html/2604.05865>
**Tier:** 1 (preprint, not peer-reviewed)
Data extracted: JTON achieves 32.2% average token savings vs JSON compact (up to 61.3%). Independent comparison: JTON 144,159 tokens (−20.2%) vs TOON 146,113 (−19.2%) vs JSON compact 180,725. LLM comprehension: +0.3pp overall across 10 models (3 improved, 3 unchanged, 3 regressed; worst regression: GPT-5.1 −8.6pp). Generation: 100% syntactic validity across 12 models. Notes TOON "is not JSON-compatible and needs a custom parser."
